A pair with no bar on a date up to the test end gets a bar at its last available close with zero volume (zero return, still ranked); the filled pairs and date ranges go to results/forward-2026-09/filled-pairs.json. Robustness run (DELISTED=drop, amendment 3): the UNFILLED data, so a pair is absent only on the dates it lacks; a held pair with no exit bar closes at its last close and is not held afterwards. Validation is untouched, so the frozen selections reproduce and the same picks are compared; results go to robustness-dropped/. It never decides.

timing: delay 1, as in v1: the signal at decision day t uses closes up to day t-1; the position is entered at the close of day t and held to the close of day t+1.

The grid and random-K selections are fixed by validation and frozen in selections.json, so they cannot use those bars; the LLM's proposals could only through the model's training data (see contamination).

selection: Within each arm, the hypothesis with the highest validation mean REBALANCED NET, the metric the gate uses; grid order breaks ties. The test split never enters a selection. Each arm also reports, as secondary and never gating, what selection on validation mean rank IC would have picked.

llm.contamination: The pinned revision 1d4bf0f2ff6012fd82039f2fa52739d0dd7c60c0 of Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B is dated 2026-08-14, the Hugging Face repository was created on 2026-08-05, and OpenRouter listed the model on 2026-08-14, all before the test window starts (2026-09-01) (evidence: results/forward-2026-09/model-evidence/). Weights published before any test-window bar existed cannot have been trained on test-window bars, so the pinned weights are not contaminated by the test window. Limitation: OpenRouter does not say which revision or quantisation it serves, and model_check compares only the id string, so this rests on OpenRouter serving that release. Record the model id, the revision and each response's model, provider and id.
llm.model_check: each response's model must be qwen/qwen3.8-27b:free or qwen/qwen3.8-27b; any other answer is refused and not recorded, and each accepted response's model, provider and id are written into the replay provenance. A failed call stops live calls (on_failure) and is never retried under another model.
llm.retirement: If the free endpoint is retired when the critic runs after 2027-08-31, the critic runs the same open weights (Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B at revision 1d4bf0f2ff6012fd82039f2fa52739d0dd7c60c0) with the same request settings on any host serving them, recorded as a deviation in DEVIATIONS.md. It never runs under a different model.

grid.hypotheses: every signal x lookback in the grid (120)

costs.gate: rebalanced, for every arm: one book held across days, traded daily back to the factor lab's unit-gross rank weights after drift; cost = 10 bps x traded notional, entry and final exit included
costs.reported_only: sleeve: every position opened and closed every day, about 20 bps a day of cost, a hurdle no slow daily signal clears; it is the loop card rule's cost and is shown, never gated on

metrics: mean daily rank IC with plain and Newey-West (Bartlett, lag 5) t-stats and one-sided p (secondary)
mean daily rebalanced net with its Newey-West t and one-sided p (primary: selects, gates, and decides)
mean daily net return per unit gross (rebalanced, and sleeve)
annualised Sharpe of daily net (x sqrt 365)
gate: Promote an arm's selection only if its test rebalanced net mean is > 0 AND > the highest test rebalanced net mean among the three baselines. The same rule for all three arms, applied by code.

verdict.rule: Computed by quantos_showcase.ablation.verdict. An arm helps only if its selection is promoted and its DAILY TEST NET has one-sided Newey-West p < 0.05. The headline comparison is paired: the LLM helps only if its arm helps and a one-sided Newey-West test on the daily LLM-minus-grid net difference, and on the daily LLM-minus-random-K difference, each has p < 0.05. Identical picks have no difference to test and do not count as a win.
verdict.newey_west_lags_note: ablation.verdict refuses a protocol whose lag differs from the lag the arms' p-values are computed with (5).

report: hypotheses tested on validation per arm and distinct overall
Bonferroni-adjusted validation p of each selection

deflated Sharpe of each selection's daily validation series (net, the selection metric): headline = the null sampling variance 1/T with the Li-Ji and Nyholt effective numbers of trials from the eigenvalues of the trials' correlation matrix, reported as a range; the full table over three variances and five trial counts as a sensitivity table, with the cells that pair a trial-Sharpe variance (already shrunk by the trials' correlation) with a reduced N flagged as double counting; descriptive, never the verdict
Holm-adjusted test p across the three arms' selections, on the verdict's p (daily net, Newey-West)
the per-hypothesis validation and test table
the range of outcomes any K-card selection could have produced

power: Stated before any LLM call, from validation data only (scripts/power_forward.py -> power.json). BREAK-EVEN thresholds, where a one-sided 5% test over one year (364 intervals; computed with 365) rejects half the time (50% power): 1.645 x (HAC sd per day) / sqrt(365). Single arm, daily net: about 8.7 bps/day for momentum-25 (7.8-9.1 across the hypotheses checked), 2.7x the best validation net (3.21). Paired LLM-minus-arm difference: 1.4-1.5 bps/day for an adjacent lookback (momentum-24 or -26 against momentum-25), 3.6-4.1 for momentum-20 or -19, 5.3 for momentum-14, 7.4 for momentum-05 and 13.7 for reversal-02. POWER: if momentum-25's true test mean equals its validation net (3.21 bps/day), the arm-level test rejects with probability about 15%; 80% power needs about 13.2 bps/day. For a neighbouring pick the paired threshold is below the arm-level one, so the arm-level test binds. Rank IC (secondary): only a mean above about 0.023 is significant. A null is the likely outcome and is reported as such.
deviations: Any departure from this file is written to results/forward-2026-09/DEVIATIONS.md before the study is scored, or, if found after, beside the results with the reason.

selection_import.why: The factor lab's last split is the only one that may end at the last available bar, so the selection-time import puts the v2 validation window (2024-01-01..2026-08-31) in that slot. A split's metrics do not depend on its slot; the scoring run refuses to proceed unless its validation numbers equal selections.json to 1e-12.

predictions.grid_ic_selection: Selecting on validation rank IC, as v2 first registered, picks reversal-02 (validation IC +0.0187, validation net -11.63 bps/day per selections.json), predicted to fail the net gate; random-K's IC pick is reversal-04 (-11.74 bps/day). That is why amendment 1 selects on net: with IC selection, 'the LLM beats the grid' would be nearly free.
predictions.net_selections: On validation net the grid picks momentum-25 (+3.21 bps/day) and random-K momentum-19 (+2.21 bps/day); both are frozen in selections.json.
predictions.ic_success_near_impossible: 0 of 120 hypotheses have positive validation net AND positive validation rank IC (power.json). Every net-selected pick has negative validation IC (momentum-25 -0.0091, momentum-19 -0.0088), so a verdict on test IC would be predicted 'does not help' for every arm whatever the LLM proposes. That is why amendment 2 tests net, the metric that selects.
